ap_statistics-m01.stem: The true value of the proportion of all voters in a city who support a measure is $0.4$. A researcher compares four estimators by simulating $1000$ samples for each and computing the estimate from every sample. The table shown gives the mean and the standard deviation of the estimates for each estimator. Which estimator is best for estimating the true value?

stimulus.description: Mean and standard deviation of the estimates from 1000 simulated samples

data.title: Results of 1000 simulated samples for each estimator

options.text: Estimator C, because the center of its sampling distribution is at the true value.
options.why: Considers bias alone; another estimator is also centered at the true value and has less variability.

options.text: Estimator D, because the center of its sampling distribution is at the true value and its spread is the smallest among the estimators that are centered there.
options.why: An estimator that is unbiased has a sampling distribution centered at the parameter, and among unbiased estimators the one with the least variability is best.

options.text: Estimator A, because it has the smallest spread of all the estimators.
options.why: Considers variability alone; the center of this sampling distribution is not at the true value, so the estimator is biased.

options.text: Estimator B, because its sampling distribution has the largest spread and so covers the most possible values.
options.why: Treats a larger spread as an advantage; more variability means estimates that are farther from the parameter more often.

blueprint.concept: Choose the best estimator from the center and spread of its simulated sampling distribution
student_thinking: Compare the center of each sampling distribution with the true value to find the unbiased estimators
Among the unbiased estimators choose the one with the smallest spread and reject choices based on only one of the two properties
